title: AI Unlocked: Sports, Media & Entertainment
blurb: For creators, journalists, clubs, and studios: production pipelines that multiply output, performance analytics, fan engagement engines, a rights-and-likeness ethics module, and a tool shoot-out across video, audio, and image AI.

modules.d: One person, studio output — what AI changes across the industry.
modules.body:
Landscape

  • Media: scripts, edits, subtitles, dubbing, thumbnails, and versioning at a fraction of legacy cost.
  • Sports: automated highlights, opposition analysis, scouting summaries, and fan content at club and creator level.
  • Entertainment: previsualization, storyboarding, music beds, localization.

The winners pair taste and access with AI throughput — this course builds the throughput.

Fei-Fei Li (The Worlds I See) reminds the industry that AI is made by people and lands on people — in media, that means audiences, athletes, and artists. Throughput without taste is noise; this course builds the throughput and trains the taste.

modules.d: Script → shoot/generate → edit → caption → thumbnail → publish, systematized.
modules.body:
Your pipeline

  • Ideation bank from audience comments; scripts with hook-first structure.
  • Edit in CapCut (auto-cuts, captions); B-roll and images via Ideogram; thumbnails A/B drafted in Canva.
  • Repurpose: one long video → shorts, article, carousel, newsletter — one prompt chain.
plAIbox™: publish a full content set (1 long + 3 shorts + article) from a single recording this week.
🧪 Interactive Lab — try it now

You are my content strategist. My channel/club: [describe audience, platform, cadence]. From this one piece of source material [paste or describe], generate a full content set: 1 long-form outline, 3 short-form scripts with 3-second hooks, 1 article draft, 2 thumbnail concepts, and a posting schedule for the week.

modules.t: Tool Study: Video, Audio & Image Shoot-Out
modules.d: Runway vs Pika vs Veo-class video; ElevenLabs vs native voices; Suno for music; access & costs.
modules.body:
Comparative snapshot

  • AI video (Runway, Pika, Google Veo-class, InVideo): short-form generation and effects; subscription tiers; strongest for b-roll, promos, previz — not yet long-form narrative.
  • Voice (ElevenLabs): best-in-class cloning/dubbing; free tier → creator plans; check consent rules before cloning any voice.
  • Music (Suno): broadcast-ready beds and jingles from prompts; free + pro tiers; read commercial-use terms per tier.
  • Images (Ideogram, Midjourney-class, Canva): Ideogram for text-in-image (posters), Canva for speed.
Access rule: match tier to usage rights — monetized content needs the plan that grants commercial license.

opts: The person’s consent and the tool’s rights terms

modules.d: Performance summaries, opposition briefs, and automated matchday media.
modules.body:
Workflows

  • Paste match data/notes → opposition brief with tactical tendencies and set-piece flags.
  • Auto-draft matchday graphics packs, recaps in two languages, and player-milestone posts.
  • Scouting: structured extraction from reports into comparable player cards.
  • Grassroots: a one-person club media team is now feasible — the Cameroon-to-anywhere playbook.

modules.d: Community engines — and the likeness, deepfake, and IP lines you never cross.
modules.body:
Engagement

  • Polls, prediction games, and AI-personalized newsletters; broadcast-list culture adapted per market.

Ethics & rights

  • Never generate a real person's likeness or voice without documented consent; label synthetic media; respect league/club IP and music licensing.
  • Disclosure norms for AI-assisted journalism: facts verified by humans, corrections policy public.

modules.t: Capstone: Your Channel or Club System
modules.d: A running media engine with metrics.
modules.body:
Capstone

  • Two weeks of published output from your pipeline, an engagement experiment with results, your tool matrix with costs/rights notes, and a 10-minute showcase to the panel.
